issues.legal_issue: An application seeking both a tenant’s ejectment and recovery of rent arrears is governed by the special land-tenure procedure when that regime prescribes the procedure for those remedies.
material_facts: The landowner applied to the Assistant Collector seeking both ejectment of the tenant and recovery of rent arrears.
The Assistant Collector followed the summary procedure prescribed for proceedings under the land-tenure regime.
issues.conclusion: The application was governed by the procedure under the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, and was not a suit under Section 77(3) of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887. The Commissioner was wrong to hold otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14-A(i) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953 requires an application to the Assistant Collector, First Grade, for ejectment, to be dealt with under Section 10(2). Section 14-A(ii) provides the procedure for recovering rent arrears, including notice to the tenant and summary determination. These provisions operate notwithstanding anything contrary in another law. The Court found that the application sought both forms of relief and that the Assistant Collector followed Section 10(2).

predicates.landowner_sought_ejectment_and_rent_reco: The landowner applied for both the tenant’s ejectment and recovery of rent arrears.
predicates.land_tenure_regime_prescribes_procedure_: The applicable land-tenure regime provides procedures for ejectment and recovery of rent arrears.
predicates.application_was_processed_under_summary_: The authority handling the application followed the summary procedure for resolving the dispute.

issues.definition: When a landowner seeks both ejectment and rent recovery, and the applicable land-tenure regime provides procedures for both remedies and the application is processed summarily, the application is governed by that regime’s procedure.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s failure to pay rent does not justify ejectment when the tenant had sufficient cause for withholding rent while pursuing a claim that, if successful, would remove the obligation to pay rent.
material_facts: The tenant withheld rent while pursuing a claim to occupancy rights in the land.
The tenant had initially obtained a decision recognizing occupancy rights, which was later reversed through the appeal and revision process.
The tenant deposited the rent while the challenge to the occupancy-rights claim was still being pursued.
The authorities’ findings that the tenant withheld rent because of the occupancy-rights claim were not disturbed.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had sufficient cause for not paying rent and was not liable to be ejected for the default.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1)(ii) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953 makes a tenant liable to ejectment for failure to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause. In Mrs. Raj Kanta v. The Financial Commissioner, Punjab and Others, (1980) 3 SCC 589, the Court explained that a tenant may avoid ejectment by proving sufficient cause for non-payment. The tenant’s pursuit of occupancy rights, which would have removed the obligation to pay rent if successful, supplied sufficient cause on these facts.

predicates.land_tenure_ejectment_proceeding: A landowner sought to eject a tenant for failing to pay rent in a proceeding governed by the land-tenure regime.
predicates.tenant_withheld_rent_while_pursuing_occu: The tenant did not pay rent while pursuing a claim to occupancy rights in the land.
predicates.successful_claim_would_remove_rent_oblig: The tenant’s occupancy-rights claim, if successful, would mean the tenant was not liable to pay rent.
predicates.tenant_deposited_rent_during_claim_proce: The tenant deposited the rent while the proceedings concerning the occupancy-rights claim were still ongoing.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a land-tenure ejectment proceeding withholds rent while pursuing an occupancy claim that would remove the rent obligation if successful, and deposits the rent during that process, the tenant is not ejectable for the rent default.
